simple.meaning: רָגַן (râgan) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to grumble , i.e. rebel.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Deuteronomy, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Deuteronomy 1:27. The surrounding contexts include land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָגַן (H7279) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רָגַן (râgan) / H7279 is traced through Deuteronomy 1:27, Psalms 106:25, Isaiah 29:24 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7279. ragan רָגַן verb murmur, whisper (Late Hebrew id. ; ᵑ7 Ithpe`el bickbite, slander ); — 1 murmur (rebelliously): — Qal Participle plural רוֺגְנִים Isa 29:24 murmurers ; Niph`al Imperfect 3masculine plural וַיֵּרָֽגְנוּ Psa 106:25 and they murmured in their tents, so 2 masculine plural וַתֵּרָֽגְנוּ Deut 1:27 . 2 whisper (maliciously), backlite, slander: , Niph`al Participle נִרְגָּן backbiter Prov 16:28 ; 18:8 ; 26:20 , 22 .

occurrences.englishText: You murmured in your tents, and said, “Because Yahweh hated us, he has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites to destroy us.
They also who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will receive instruction.”
